# `.apkg` and `.colpkg` test fixtures

Generated by `tool/make_apkg_fixtures.py` with the official `anki` Python
package (built with Anki 26.09.3). Do not edit these files by hand.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `modern.apkg` | Current format: `collection.anki21b` (zstd), zstd protobuf `media` map, zstd-compressed media files. |
| `legacy.apkg` | Exported with "support older Anki versions": `collection.anki21`, JSON `media` map, plain media files. Same content as `modern.apkg`. |
| `truncated.apkg` | The first half of `modern.apkg`, a corrupt package. |
| `modern.colpkg` | The whole collection in the current format (`collection.anki21b` plus Anki's dummy `collection.anki2`), with an empty deck and a filtered deck added (see below). |
| `legacy.colpkg` | The same collection, exported with "support older Anki versions" (`collection.anki21`). |
| `truncated.colpkg` | The first half of `modern.colpkg`, a corrupt package. |
| `update-v1.apkg`, `update-v1-legacy.apkg`, `update-v2.apkg`, `update-v3.apkg` | One small shared deck at three points in time, for re-importing with an update policy (see below). The legacy twin of version 1 uses `collection.anki21`. |
| `latex.apkg`, `latex-legacy.apkg` | A deck with pre-generated LaTeX images, in the current and the legacy format (see below). |
| `occlusion.apkg`, `occlusion-legacy.apkg` | A deck of Image Occlusion notes, in the current and the legacy format (see below). |
| `fixtures.json` | Normalised content of all four packages, read straight from them (presets with Anki's values and enums). Tests use it as expected values. For the collection packages it lists every deck and note type; a card in a filtered deck has `homeDeck` and `homeDue`. |

Both packages contain the decks `Fixture`, `Fixture::Spanish` and
`Fixture::Geo`, with eight notes (fixed GUIDs, prefix `cf-`) and twelve cards:

- `Fixture::Spanish` uses its own deck options preset, `Fixture Spanish`, with every option the importer maps set away from Anki's defaults; the other decks use Anki's default preset.
- Basic notes, one of them with an image (`dog.png`, `cat.jpg`), and custom CSS on the note type.
- A `Basic (and reversed card)` note (two new cards); the forward card has the green flag (3).
- A Cloze note with a hint, `{{c1::Paris::city}} … {{c2::France}}`; card 1 is in learning.
- A Cloze note with a multi-number deletion, `{{c1,2::Paris}} is in {{c3::France}}` (three new cards).
- Two notes with `[sound:…]` tags and audio media (`hola.mp3`, `adios.mp3`) (imported since audio playback was added).
- A review card with an FSRS memory state (`cf-basic-hola`, due day 300, ivl 15).
- A suspended review card without a memory state (`cf-basic-cat`, ease 230 %).
- Review history (`revlog`) for three cards, all dated before 2026-09-22
  (Anki refuses to export entries dated in the future):
  - `cf-basic-hola`: 12 entries, with learning, reviews, a lapse and relearning, a review in a filtered deck that reschedules (type 3) and a set due date (type 5, ease 0).
  - `cf-basic-cat`: 8 learning and review entries under SM-2, without an FSRS memory state.
  - `cf-cloze-paris` card 1: learning, a cram review (type 3, factor 0), a reset to new (type 4, ease 0, interval 0), then learning again.

After the `.apkg` exports, two decks are added for the collection packages:
the empty deck `Inbox::Later` (with its parent `Inbox`), and the filtered deck
`Filtered Nouns`, which pulls `cf-basic-dog` out of `Fixture::Spanish`. The
collection packages also contain Anki's `Default` deck and its stock note types,
used or not.

The update packages hold the deck `Update Fixture` with the note type
`Update Vocab` (`Front`, `Back`). Unlike the other packages, their note and
note type modification times are fixed, and `fixtures.json` lists them under
`updates`:

- Version 1 (2026-03-01): `cf-up-hola` (`hola` / `helo`, a typo) and `cf-up-gato`.
- Version 2 (2026-04-01): the typo in `cf-up-hola` is fixed (`hello`) and the note type's CSS changed; `cf-up-gato` is untouched and keeps its time.
- Version 3 (2026-05-01): the note type gains the field `Audio`, shown on the back; `cf-up-hola` gets an `Audio` value and the new note `cf-up-perro` is added. Adding the field gave every note the new time.

The LaTeX packages hold the deck `Latex Fixture` with two note types,
`Latex PNG` (Anki's default PNG images) and `Latex SVG` (set to SVG images,
`latexsvg`), both with `Front` and `Back`:

- `cf-latex-png`: `[latex]a<br>b &amp; <b>c</b>[/latex]` on the front, `[$]x^2[/$] and [$$]\sum_i i[/$$]` on the back.
- `cf-latex-missing`: `[latex]\LaTeX[/latex]`, whose image is not in the media.
- `cf-latex-svg` (SVG): `[$]E = mc^2[/$]`, and `[$$]\frac{1}{2}&nbsp;<i>x</i>[/$$]` on the back.

There is no TeX installation, so the images are small placeholder PNG and SVG
files. Their names (`latex-<sha1>.png` or `.svg`) come from Anki, which also
picked them for the export; `fixtures.json` lists them per note and field
under `latex.names`.

The occlusion packages hold the deck `Occlusion Fixture` with Anki's stock
`Image Occlusion` note type (fields `Occlusion`, `Image`, `Header`,
`Back Extra`, `Comments`), the notes added with Anki's own
`add_image_occlusion_note`. Both notes show the image `diagram.png`
(40×24 pixels, so x and y scale differently); `fixtures.json` lists them
under `occlusion`:

- `cf-io-all`, "Hide all, guess one" (`oi=1` on every shape), three cards: a
  rectangle (c1), a rotated ellipse (c2), a polygon and a rectangle grouped
  as c3, and a text label (c0), which is always shown and makes no card.
  Header `Heart`, Back Extra `Anatomy`.
- `cf-io-one`, "Hide one, guess one" (no `oi`): two rectangles, two cards.

The collection creation time (`crt`) is fixed at 2026-01-01 04:00 UTC, so review
due days are stable, and review log IDs are fixed. Anki assigns note and card IDs
and modification times from the clock, so the package bytes change between runs
while their content does not.

Regenerate, or check that a fresh build has identical content:

```sh
pip install anki
tool/make_apkg_fixtures.py          # rewrite the fixtures
tool/make_apkg_fixtures.py --check  # exit 0 when regenerated content is identical
```
